added_failures_note: the reviewed run records no baseline_suite or after_suite pair: it is a measurement node whose suite fence is unarmed

0.reason: the live-MCP postcondition runs after landing on the promoted code; the coordinator runs roadmap through the restarted MCP server and records the result in the plan

1.reason: summary-script labelling: the base arm is a control and carries no target of its own; the gate log's verdicts are per arm

findings.summary: The plan's §6 done-when activates a live-MCP postcondition once every target is met — roadmap(project="reckon") through the MCP server, restarted on the promoted code, returns without storage-slow — and the fragment records only in-process mcp._roadmap() calls, so the deadline wrapper (reckon/_mcp_tools.py:9, reckon/mcp_deadlines.py) that turns a blocked read into storage-slow was never exercised; the run's own manifest records rubric.mcp_postcondition as NOT answered.

TARGETS is keyed by (read, phase) only, so the head arm's warm-audit 3 s target is applied to the base arm and measure/core/sbatch.log:28 prints "audit | base | warm | 3 | 4.468 | 3.0 | MISSED" against a target the plan assigns to the head arm only; the plan, measure/gate.log:31 says that cell carries no target.

The glob includes every *-build.log, so the summary's medians are taken over four samples (the untargeted build warm-up plus three rounds) and disagree with the gate log's three-round medians: measure/core/sbatch.log:33 reports roadmap head cold 7.526 at n=4 while measure/gate.log:23 and the fragment report 7.481 at n=3.

review_text:
VERDICT goal: the goal is to measure roadmap, audit and discovery reads cold and warm on a frozen corpus against their deadlines; docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/the-reads-are-measured-inside-their-deadline.html:29-40 records all six medians per arm and marks the three targets.
VERDICT done_when: the done-when's log clause is met by measure/gate.log:16-33 (medians beside the §1 figures, targets marked, both jobs EXIT=0 at :56-57), but its live-MCP clause, roadmap(project="reckon") through the MCP server restarted on the promoted code, was not run.
VERDICT write_paths: the node's single declared path is the one file the diff adds, docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/the-reads-are-measured-inside-their-deadline.html; the dumps, corpus revision and logs the done-when requires sit under the run's own directory.
VERDICT manifest: read; status complete, commits b8a9fc24f2 and 339d0e7f, the tests line names the two sbatch measurement jobs as the gate, and rubric.mcp_postcondition is recorded NOT answered.
VERDICT diff: two commits against b4700c0d read commit by commit; the first rewrote the fragment and the second replaced it, both touching only that file for 111 added lines and no code or test.
CALL_SITES: reckon/evidence.py:687 compose_landed_record, reckon/serve.py:2705, reckon/mcp.py:1344, reckon/doccheck.py:1970
SCORE goal_fidelity: 17
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/the-reads-are-measured-inside-their-deadline.html:29-40 tabulates every read, arm and phase with its median and verdict, which is what the goal names.
SCORE evidence: 15
JUSTIFICATION evidence: measure/gate.log:16-33 records the three targeted medians beside the §1 figures and both jobs exited 0, but the done-when's live-MCP clause is unrun and measure/core/sbatch.log:28-33 disagrees with that table.
SCORE scope_discipline: 19
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: the diff adds exactly one file, docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/the-reads-are-measured-inside-their-deadline.html, which is the node's declared write path.
SCORE durability: 10
JUSTIFICATION durability: the diff adds no assertion and no repository test, so nothing in the repo fails if this measurement regresses; the only guard is the instrument check at measure/arm.py:23-64 (ok=False on an error or empty answer, EXIT=3 outside the code tree), which lives in the run directory.
SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: the fragment opens with the same article class="landed-report" data-run-id/data-node wrapper as its sibling docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/a-read-takes-no-lock.html and introduces no plan, sprint or version label.
SCORE reuse: 20
JUSTIFICATION reuse: the diff adds no function, class or module; the fragment is data consumed by the existing composer reckon/evidence.py:687, so no repository capability is forked.
